title: A proper closed subscheme supports all terms of a coherent formal system
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal such that $A$ is $I$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Let $f:X\to S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] and of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For $n\geq0$ put $S_n=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I^{n+1})$ and $X_n=X\times_S S_n$ [def-pc-base-change], and let $j_n:X_n\to X$ and $i_n:X_n\to X_{n+1}$ be the canonical closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Pullback is tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]; coherent modules are as in [pqf-def-coherent]. Let $F_n$ be coherent $\mathcal O_{X_n}$-modules with isomorphisms $\varphi_n:i_n^*F_{n+1}\cong F_n$. Suppose $\operatorname{Supp}(F_0)$ is proper over $S_0$ [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base]. Then there is a closed immersion $j:Z\to X$ with $Z\to S$ proper such that $\mathcal J_Z$ annihilates every $j_{n,*}F_n$. Explicitly, for every $n\geq0$, open $V\subseteq X$, section $a\in\mathcal J_Z(V)$ and $t\in(j_{n,*}F_n)(V)$, one has $at=0$.

proof.text: Package the coherent terms and transitions as CoherentThickeningSystem. The dictionary supplies X Noetherian, a coherent formal module, the evaluation isomorphisms with the pushed terms, and the proper first support equivalence.

For a formal module define P to mean annihilation by a proper closed subscheme and R to mean proper first support. Both predicates are Serre classes. Every term is quasi-coherent by coherence on the Noetherian scheme. Applying the affine-cover ideal-product vanishing criterion at exponent one to the zero ideal proves that the zero ideal annihilates every term.

If P fails for the given R-object, the set S of ideals killing an R-object for which P fails contains the zero ideal. Apply the maximal-ideal clause of noetherian_quasicoherent_submodules to obtain K maximal in S and T killed by K with R(T) and not P(T). Use the coherent first term of the given system as the ambient coherent module in that theorem.

The Chow comparison supplies N with P(N), alpha:T -> N, and J>K killing kernel alpha. Serre subobject closure gives R(kernel alpha). If P failed for the kernel then J would belong to S, contradicting maximality of K. Hence P(kernel alpha). Apply the Serre-class exact-sequence lemma to kernel alpha -> T -> N, which is exact by the kernel universal property, to conclude P(T), a contradiction. The cokernel is never needed. Normalize the zero-morphism structure by its uniqueness in the generic categorical helper.

For each term supported on the proper closed subscheme, apply coherent closed-immersion equivalence and its counit to identify it with a pushed coherent module on that subscheme. Closed pushforward is sectionwise annihilated by the ideal. Compose this identification with the dictionary evaluation isomorphism. Linearity, the inverse-isomorphism identity on sections, and preservation of zero transfer the scalar equation to the original pushed thickening term on every open.

proof_origin.place: Theorem 088E and Remark 088F. Formalized maximal failing-ideal argument and dictionary transfer; the geometric comparison is split off. Serre closure applied directly to the exact kernel sequence eliminates the cokernel branch.
